records.name: Smolensk Oblast
records.summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no region-specific trans-related evidence for it: hostility here is legislated federally and administered by federal security services, so the division inherits the national picture (score 0.12; deviation vs national ±0.02). The federal layer applying here: the 2023 ban on legal gender recognition and gender-affirming care; the propaganda law (up to 15 days' detention plus deportation for foreign visitors who 'promote' non-traditional relationships); the 'LGBT extremism' designation regime (101 convictions, 146 fines in 2024); and uncorrectable document markers, so any police, hotel or transport identity check reads a mismatch.

records.name: Tuva
records.summary:
No division-specific transgender evidence appears in the surviving sources; a visitor here stands under the national framework as it operates countrywide.

As those sources establish: same-sex activity is not criminalised, but the 2023 laws ban same-sex marriage and legal gender recognition; the 'extremism' designation has produced 101 convictions since early 2024, with 'propaganda' penalties surging to 257 in 2023-24; official asylum guidance singles out trans people, open activists and one conflict-affected region cluster for heightened risk.
